note: The 20-pattern taxonomy. Folder id is the sort order and the dependency order — do not renumber without regenerating curriculum/track.md. 'signals' are what a learner should spot in a problem STATEMENT to select this pattern; they are the raw material for the S1 gate. 'depends_on' gates curriculum sequencing.

patterns.name: Arrays & Hashing
patterns.core_idea: Trade space for time. A lookup table turns 'have I seen this?' from a scan into a constant-time question.
signals: asks for duplicates, counts, or frequencies
asks whether two collections contain the same elements
you catch yourself writing a nested loop whose inner loop only searches
order does not matter in the answer
patterns.invariant_shape: The table always holds every element seen so far, and nothing else.
common_traps: using a list where a set would do, keeping the O(n) lookup
counting characters but forgetting the alphabet is bounded

patterns.name: Two Pointers
patterns.core_idea: On sorted or symmetric data, two indices moving toward each other examine every useful pair without examining all pairs.
signals: input is sorted, or sorting it loses nothing
asks for a pair or triplet meeting a condition
palindrome or mirror structure
asks to partition or dedupe in place
patterns.invariant_shape: Everything outside [left, right] has already been decided and will never need revisiting.
common_traps: moving both pointers when only one should move
forgetting to skip duplicates and emitting the same triplet twice

patterns.name: Sliding Window
patterns.core_idea: A contiguous range that grows on the right and shrinks on the left, so each element is added once and removed once.
signals: asks for a contiguous subarray or substring
asks for longest/shortest/max/min subject to a condition
a condition that can be broken by adding and repaired by removing
patterns.invariant_shape: The window always satisfies the condition (or is the smallest violation), and the answer so far is the best window seen.
common_traps: shrinking with an if when a while is needed
recomputing the window's state instead of updating it incrementally

patterns.name: Binary Search
patterns.core_idea: Halve a search space that has a monotonic yes/no property. The array need not be the search space.
signals: sorted input
constraints large enough that O(n) per query is too slow
asks for the minimum value that works or maximum that still works
you can write a cheap check(x) that is false then true
patterns.invariant_shape: The answer is always inside [lo, hi]; every discarded half provably cannot contain it.
common_traps: infinite loop from the wrong mid rounding
searching on the array when you should search on the answer range

patterns.name: Stack
patterns.core_idea: Last-in-first-out matches any structure where the most recent unresolved thing must resolve first.
signals: nesting, brackets, or matched pairs
undo, backtrack, or 'most recent'
expression parsing
simulating recursion iteratively
patterns.invariant_shape: The stack holds exactly the opened-but-not-yet-closed items, innermost on top.
common_traps: popping an empty stack
checking balance only by count, ignoring type and order

patterns.name: Monotonic Stack
patterns.core_idea: A stack kept sorted discards elements that can never be the answer, giving next-greater / previous-smaller in linear time.
signals: asks for next greater, next smaller, or span
histogram, rainwater, or skyline shapes
a nested loop scanning forward for the first element bigger than the current
patterns.invariant_shape: The stack is monotonic; anything popped was made irrelevant by the element that popped it.
common_traps: storing values when you need indices to compute width
wrong strictness, so equal elements are handled twice or not at all

patterns.name: Linked List
patterns.core_idea: Pointer surgery. You cannot index, so you keep exactly the references you need and rewire carefully.
signals: input is a linked list
asks to reverse, merge, reorder, or remove in place
O(1) space demanded on a list
patterns.invariant_shape: At each step the processed prefix is fully rewired and the unprocessed suffix is still intact and reachable.
common_traps: losing the rest of the list by reassigning next too early
no dummy head, so the head case needs special handling

patterns.name: Fast & Slow Pointers
patterns.core_idea: Two pointers at different speeds meet iff there is a cycle, and their meeting point locates structure.
signals: cycle detection
find the middle in one pass
find the nth from the end
a repeated value hidden in a range, framed as a sequence
patterns.invariant_shape: Fast has always travelled exactly twice slow's distance.
common_traps: null dereference when checking fast and fast.next in the wrong order
stopping at detection when the question wants the cycle entry

patterns.name: Trees (DFS & BFS)
patterns.core_idea: Recursion mirrors the structure. Decide what each node needs from its children, and what it returns to its parent.
signals: input is a binary tree or n-ary tree
depth, path, ancestor, or level
asks to validate or compare structure
patterns.invariant_shape: Each recursive call returns a correct answer for its whole subtree, assuming its children did.
common_traps: validating a BST against the parent instead of a propagated range
confusing depth with height

patterns.name: Tries
patterns.core_idea: A tree keyed by character shares prefixes, so prefix questions cost the length of the word, not the size of the dictionary.
signals: prefix search or autocomplete
many words queried against one dictionary
wildcard matching over a word set
patterns.invariant_shape: Every path from the root spells a prefix of at least one inserted word.
common_traps: no end-of-word marker, so prefixes match as whole words
rebuilding the trie per query

patterns.name: Heap / Top-K
patterns.core_idea: You rarely need full order. A size-k heap keeps only the candidates that can still win.
signals: asks for k largest, k smallest, k most frequent
asks for a running median or a stream
merging many sorted sources
patterns.invariant_shape: The heap holds the best k seen so far; its root is the weakest of those k.
common_traps: min-heap vs max-heap inverted for the question asked
sorting everything when a size-k heap was enough

patterns.name: Backtracking
patterns.core_idea: Enumerate a decision tree, undoing each choice on the way out so the state is clean for the next branch.
signals: asks for all combinations, permutations, subsets, or valid arrangements
small n with a factorial or exponential answer space
constraint satisfaction — sudoku, n-queens, word search
patterns.invariant_shape: On entering a node the state reflects exactly the choices on the path from the root; on leaving, it is restored.
common_traps: appending a reference to the mutable path instead of a copy
forgetting to undo the choice after recursing

patterns.name: Graphs
patterns.core_idea: A tree with cycles. Everything from trees applies, plus you must remember what you have already visited.
signals: grid, matrix, islands, or regions
nodes and edges, prerequisites, connections
shortest path in an unweighted graph
cycle detection or ordering with dependencies
patterns.invariant_shape: Every node is enqueued at most once; visited is marked at enqueue time, not dequeue time.
common_traps: marking visited on dequeue, so a node enters the queue many times
treating an undirected edge as one-directional

patterns.name: Advanced Graphs
patterns.core_idea: Weighted and structured graph algorithms: Dijkstra, MST, union-find with compression, topological order with counts.
signals: edges carry weights or costs
asks for cheapest path or cheapest way to connect everything
asks to detect cycles across merges
patterns.invariant_shape: Once a node is finalized its distance is optimal and never changes.
common_traps: Dijkstra on negative weights
union-find without rank or path compression, degrading to a linked list

patterns.name: Intervals
patterns.core_idea: Sort by one endpoint, then a single sweep decides overlap with only the previous interval in hand.
signals: input is pairs of start and end
asks to merge, insert, or count overlaps
meeting rooms, calendars, bookings
patterns.invariant_shape: After sorting, everything before the current interval is already merged and final.
common_traps: sorting by end when the question needs start (or the reverse)
off-by-one on whether touching endpoints count as overlapping

patterns.name: Greedy
patterns.core_idea: A locally best choice is globally optimal — but only when you can argue why. The argument is the work.
signals: asks for a minimum number of steps or maximum profit
jump games, gas stations, scheduling
an exchange argument works: swapping toward the greedy choice never hurts
patterns.invariant_shape: The partial solution is extendable to an optimal one at every step.
common_traps: assuming greedy works without checking a counterexample
greedy on a problem that needs DP because choices interact

patterns.name: 1-D Dynamic Programming
patterns.core_idea: Overlapping subproblems. Define the state, write the recurrence, then stop recomputing.
signals: asks for count of ways, min cost, or max value
brute force is exponential and recomputes the same subproblem
the choice at step i depends only on a bounded number of earlier steps
patterns.invariant_shape: dp[i] is the answer to the problem restricted to the first i elements, and is computed only from strictly smaller indices.
common_traps: state that does not capture enough to make the recurrence correct
base case off by one, or wrong iteration direction

patterns.name: 2-D Dynamic Programming
patterns.core_idea: Two indices in the state — usually two sequences, or one sequence plus a budget.
signals: two strings compared
a grid with paths
a knapsack-shaped budget or capacity
patterns.invariant_shape: dp[i][j] answers the subproblem on the first i of one dimension and first j of the other.
common_traps: iterating in an order where a needed cell is not yet filled
rolling to 1-D too early and clobbering a value still needed

patterns.name: Bit Manipulation
patterns.core_idea: Integers as fixed-width arrays of bits. XOR cancels, AND masks, shifts move.
signals: asks to do it without extra space or without arithmetic operators
counting set bits, single number among pairs
subsets encoded as a bitmask
patterns.invariant_shape: Each bit position is independent and can be reasoned about alone.
common_traps: sign extension on right shift for negative numbers
assuming 32 bits in a language with arbitrary-precision integers

patterns.name: Math & Geometry
patterns.core_idea: The structure of the numbers or the plane is the shortcut. Find the property, skip the simulation.
signals: matrix rotation or spiral traversal
digits, primes, gcd, modular arithmetic
overflow explicitly mentioned in constraints
patterns.invariant_shape: A stated mathematical property holds at every step and is what makes the shortcut valid.
common_traps: integer overflow on intermediate products
in-place rotation applied twice to the same cell
